candidates.source_agent: Relatability Ethnographer; repaired by full room
candidates.title: The Packet Pause
candidates.one_line_concept: During each other's calls or voice notes, Aachu and Zuv freeze mid-snack-opening, mid-spoon-clink, or mid-cup-place because certain household sounds are apparently illegal now.
candidates.emotional_truth: Love is ridiculous self-control for exactly the sound that would ruin the other person's moment.
candidates.humor_angle: A snack packet becomes a threat object.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Couples who know the panic of making one loud sound during a partner's call.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Babe this is you opening chips during my meeting.
candidates.visual_potential: Laptop call, half-torn snack packet, frozen guilty body, tea/cup/spoon echo beat, clean negative space.
candidates.why_people_may_share: It lets one partner lovingly accuse the other of being either the loud-snack person or the silent-packet specialist.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Comment bait: chip packets, steel spoons, mixer grinders, doors, and every sound that becomes louder during calls.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Low if staged around specific sound objects and mutual call etiquette.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: love is knowing which sounds are illegal during a call.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: 4 slides: first call, frozen packet, role reversal, payoff where they open/eat together after the call.

candidates.title: The Door Was Never Fully Closed
candidates.one_line_concept: After a small fight, one of them goes to the other room but leaves the door slightly open, because the argument needs distance but love does not.
candidates.emotional_truth: Real couples perform being angry while secretly keeping a path back open.
candidates.humor_angle: A dramatic exit with a re-entry policy.
candidates.relatable_trigger: The partner whose sulk still leaves a tiny invitation.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: You literally do this when you are mad.
candidates.visual_potential: Half-open bedroom door, strip of light, two separated readable figures.
candidates.why_people_may_share: It names a private repair signal after a petty fight.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Comments about leaving doors open, loud sighs, and fake anger.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium-low; can become too sad if not petty and domestic.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: 4 slides: fight residue, open door, almost-apology object, return.

candidates.title: The Real Date Starts After We Leave
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu and Zuv leave a social thing and immediately begin the private couple debrief.
candidates.emotional_truth: Being a team sometimes means saving the real conversation for the ride home.
candidates.humor_angle: The debrief face starts before the door has closed.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Couples who need 45 minutes to process a 2-hour outing.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: This is us after meeting anyone.
candidates.visual_potential: Car/scooter/walk-home debrief, shoes off at doorway, shared glance.
candidates.why_people_may_share: Private social-event debriefs are deeply taggable.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Who starts the debrief first and how long does yours last?
candidates.suggested_text_hook: the real date starts after we leave.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: 4 slides: public smiles, exit, private debrief face, laughing together.

candidates.title: The Charger Has A Favorite Person
candidates.one_line_concept: One long charging cable keeps migrating toward whoever is pretending they do not need attention.
candidates.emotional_truth: Sometimes the prop reveals that both people wanted to sit closer anyway.
candidates.humor_angle: The charger is blamed for their proximity.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Couples with one long charger and no personal space.
candidates.visual_potential: Single cable crossing room, phones at low battery, both ending beside one outlet.
candidates.why_people_may_share: Shared charger politics are common and lightly accusatory.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Cable length, battery percentage, outlet corner confessions.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium-low; needs intimacy not tech complaint.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: the charger has a favorite person.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: 4 slides: missing cable, cable migration, outlet corner, phones abandoned.

candidates.title: The Subtitles Came On Without Discussion
candidates.one_line_concept: One person is eating something too crunchy during a movie, so the other silently turns subtitles on instead of starting a fight.
candidates.emotional_truth: Soft partnership is choosing the workaround before the complaint.
candidates.humor_angle: Crunchy snacks become an accessibility setting.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Movie-night couples with loud snacks and quiet peace treaties.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: You are the reason subtitles are on.
candidates.visual_potential: Sofa, remote, snack bowl, subtitles implied without readable TV text.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: i turned subtitles on for your chips.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: 3-4 slides: crunch, side-eye, remote click, peaceful movie night.

candidates.title: Assigned Seats, Denied Publicly
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu and Zuv insist they are normal people, but the sofa, cafe bench, and bed all know exactly whose side is whose.
candidates.emotional_truth: Long-term intimacy turns space into an unspoken map.
candidates.humor_angle: They deny assigned seats while obeying them perfectly.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Couples with sacred sides of the sofa, bed, or cafe bench.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Do not sit on my side.
candidates.visual_potential: Three repeated seat claims across home/cafe/bed, or one sofa scene with territorial body language.
candidates.why_people_may_share: It lets people lovingly call out the partner who steals or protects a spot.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium; needs fresh staging beyond a sofa.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: we don't have assigned seats. we absolutely have assigned seats.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: 3-4 slides: denial, repeated seat proof, stolen spot, surrender.

candidates.title: The Remote Control Custody Battle
candidates.one_line_concept: The remote keeps changing hands, but the real joke is that neither of them is actually watching anymore.
candidates.emotional_truth: Some couple arguments are rituals for staying engaged with each other.
candidates.humor_angle: The remote is a courtroom exhibit.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Couples who negotiate TV control more seriously than the show deserves.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: We fight for the remote and then talk over the show.
candidates.visual_potential: Sofa, remote, snack bowl peace offering, TV menu implied.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium; sitcom risk unless the handoff rituals feel intimate.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: we fought for the remote and watched each other instead.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: 4 slides: claim, negotiation, abandoned remote, laughing payoff.

candidates.title: No-Context Screenshot Department
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu sends Zuv a screenshot with only 'thoughts?' and he somehow understands the full emotional, financial, aesthetic, and future-life context.
candidates.emotional_truth: A real couple builds a private shorthand where one tiny prompt carries a whole world.
candidates.humor_angle: Thoughts? is treated as a complete briefing document.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Couples with unexplained screenshots and instant decoding rituals.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: I send screenshots like court evidence.
candidates.visual_potential: Phone as trigger, then room decision: chair, outfit, cart, plant, or menu choice.
candidates.why_people_may_share: Modern couple shorthand is taggable with zero explanation.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium-high; too phone-led unless story room grounds it in a physical decision.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: relationship stage: 'thoughts?' is a complete sentence.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: 4 slides: screenshot arrives, Zuv decodes, real object decision, no-context reply becomes enough.

candidates.title: Fan Speed 2.5
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu and Zuv negotiate the fan, blanket, window, and one-foot-out compromise like two diplomats trying to sleep in the same weather system.
candidates.emotional_truth: Sharing a life means making peace with a body that experiences weather differently.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Couples with fan-speed politics and blanket treaties.
candidates.visual_potential: Bedroom fan, blanket tug, one foot out, window half-open.
candidates.why_people_may_share: Temperature conflict is daily and warmly accusatory.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Fan speed teams and blanket-in-June teams.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: true love is agreeing on fan speed 2.5.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: 3-4 slides: fan dispute, blanket treaty, one-foot compromise, sleep peace.

candidates.title: The Correct Bite Treaty
candidates.one_line_concept: They both pretend to eat normally, but each keeps saving the best corner of the snack for the other.
candidates.emotional_truth: Intimacy is knowing which bite is the good bite and giving it away without announcing the sacrifice.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Couples with serious unspoken food negotiations.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: I say I am full and then stare.
candidates.visual_potential: One plate, best corner, nudged bite, split crumb payoff.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Last-bite liar, martyr, and thief confessions.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium; food sharing can become cute-card fast.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: we don't split the last bite. we hold negotiations.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: 3-4 slides: pretend generosity, nudged bite, standoff, absurd split.
